title: Impact of Credit Score Threshold on Loan Default Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)**

This is a classic RDD setup. The running variable is the credit score, and there is a sharp cutoff threshold that determines treatment (loan approval). Individuals just above the threshold receive treatment (loan approval, `treated=1`), while those just below do not.

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **No precise manipulation of the running variable:** Borrowers cannot precisely manipulate their credit scores to sort just above/below the threshold. This is testable via a McCrary density test.
2. **Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff:** In the absence of treatment, default rates would evolve smoothly through the threshold. This means any discontinuous jump in `y` at the cutoff is attributable to crossing the threshold.
3. **Local randomization:** Near the cutoff, individuals just above and just below are comparable in all respects except treatment assignment.

The cutoff appears to be at 0.5 based on the data preview (treated=1 when running_var > 0.5). The causal estimand is the Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) at the cutoff.

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# RDD Analysis: Credit Score Threshold and Loan Default Rates
# ============================================================

# Load libraries
if (!require("rdrobust")) install.packages("rdrobust", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
if (!require("rddensity")) install.packages("rddensity", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)

# Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s89_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
str(df)
summary(df)
cat("\nN observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("N treated:", sum(df$treated), "\n")
cat("N control:", sum(df$treated == 0), "\n")

# ============================================================
# Step 1: Identify the cutoff
# ============================================================
# Determine cutoff from data: the minimum running_var among treated
cutoff_candidates <- c(
  max(df$running_var[df$treated == 0]),
  min(df$running_var[df$treated == 1])
)
cutoff <- mean(cutoff_candidates)
cat("\nEstimated cutoff (midpoint):", cutoff, "\n")

# More likely the cutoff is exactly 0.5 — verify
cat("Max running_var among untreated:", max(df$running_var[df$treated == 0]), "\n")
cat("Min running_var among treated:", min(df$running_var[df$treated == 1]), "\n")

# Check if 0.5 is a clean cutoff
if (all(df$treated[df$running_var > 0.5] == 1) & all(df$treated[df$running_var <= 0.5] == 0)) {
  cutoff <- 0.5
  cat("Confirmed: Sharp cutoff at 0.5\n")
} else {
  cat("Cutoff may not be exactly 0.5, using estimated:", cutoff, "\n")
}

# Center the running variable
df$X <- df$running_var - cutoff

# ============================================================
# Step 2: Visualization
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Visual Inspection: Mean Y by bins ===\n")
df$bin <- cut(df$X, breaks = 20)
bin_means <- aggregate(y ~ bin, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(bin_means)

# ============================================================
# Step 3: McCrary Density Test (Manipulation Test)
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== McCrary Density Test ===\n")
density_test <- rddensity(df$running_var, c = cutoff)
cat("Density test p-value:", density_test$test$p_jk, "\n")
if (density_test$test$p_jk > 0.05) {
  cat("PASS: No evidence of manipulation at the cutoff.\n")
} else {
  cat("WARNING: Evidence of potential manipulation at the cutoff.\n")
}

# ============================================================
# Step 4: Main RDD Estimation using rdrobust
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Main RDD Estimation (rdrobust) ===\n")
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff)
summary(rd_main)

cat("\n--- Key Results ---\n")
cat("RDD Estimate (LATE):", rd_main$coef[1], "\n")
cat("Robust 95% CI: [", rd_main$ci[3,1], ",", rd_main$ci[3,2], "]\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", rd_main$pv[3], "\n")
cat("Bandwidth (h):", rd_main$bws[1,1], "\n")
cat("Effective N (left):", rd_main$N_h[1], "\n")
cat("Effective N (right):", rd_main$N_h[2], "\n")

# ============================================================
# Step 5: Robustness Check 1 — Different bandwidths
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Half and Double Bandwidth ===\n")

h_main <- rd_main$bws[1,1]

# Half bandwidth
rd_half <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h_main / 2)
cat("Half bandwidth (h =", h_main/2, "):\n")
cat("  Estimate:", rd_half$coef[1], "\n")
cat("  Robust p-value:", rd_half$pv[3], "\n")

# Double bandwidth
rd_double <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h_main * 2)
cat("Double bandwidth (h =", h_main*2, "):\n")
cat("  Estimate:", rd_double$coef[1], "\n")
cat("  Robust p-value:", rd_double$pv[3], "\n")

# ============================================================
# Step 6: Robustness Check 2 — Different polynomial orders
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Different Polynomial Orders ===\n")

for (p in 1:3) {
  rd_p <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = p)
  cat("Polynomial order", p, ": Estimate =", rd_p$coef[1],
      ", Robust p-value =", rd_p$pv[3], "\n")
}

# ============================================================
# Step 7: Robustness Check 3 — Different kernel functions
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Different Kernels ===\n")
for (kern in c("triangular", "epanechnikov", "uniform")) {
  rd_k <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, kernel = kern)
  cat("Kernel:", kern, ": Estimate =", rd_k$coef[1],
      ", Robust p-value =", rd_k$pv[3], "\n")
}

# ============================================================
# Step 8: Parametric RDD as additional check
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Parametric Local Linear Regression ===\n")

# Narrow window around cutoff
bw <- h_main
df_local <- df[abs(df$X) <= bw, ]
cat("Observations in bandwidth:", nrow(df_local), "\n")

# Local linear regression
model_linear <- lm(y ~ treated * X, data = df_local)
cat("\nLocal Linear Model:\n")
print(summary(model_linear))
cat("\nParametric RDD estimate:", coef(model_linear)["treated"], "\n")

# Quadratic
model_quad <- lm(y ~ treated * poly(X, 2, raw = TRUE), data = df_local)
cat("\nLocal Quadratic Model:\n")
cat("Parametric RDD estimate (quadratic):", coef(model_quad)["treated"], "\n")

# ============================================================
# Step 9: Placebo tests at fake cutoffs
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Placebo Tests at False Cutoffs ===\n")
placebo_cutoffs <- c(0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.7)
for (pc in placebo_cutoffs) {
  tryCatch({
    rd_placebo <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = pc)
    cat("Placebo cutoff at", pc, ": Estimate =", rd_placebo$coef[1],
        ", Robust p-value =", rd_placebo$pv[3], "\n")
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Placebo cutoff at", pc, ": Could not estimate -", e$message, "\n")
  })
}

# ============================================================
# Summary
# ============================================================
cat("\n============================================\n")
cat("SUMMARY OF FINDINGS\n")
cat("============================================\n")
cat("Cutoff:", cutoff, "\n")
cat("Main RDD Estimate (LATE):", rd_main$coef[1], "\n")
cat("Conventional SE:", rd_main$se[1], "\n")
cat("Robust 95% CI: [", rd_main$ci[3,1], ",", rd_main$ci[3,2], "]\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", rd_main$pv[3], "\n")
cat("Optimal bandwidth:", rd_main$bws[1,1], "\n")

if (rd_main$pv[3] < 0.05) {
  cat("\nCONCLUSION: Statistically significant discontinuity at the cutoff.\n")
  if (rd_main$coef[1] > 0) {
    cat("Crossing the threshold INCREASES default rates by approximately",
        round(rd_main$coef[1], 4), "units.\n")
  } else {
    cat("Crossing the threshold DECREASES default rates by approximately",
        round(abs(rd_main$coef[1]), 4), "units.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("\nCONCLUSION: No statistically significant discontinuity at the cutoff.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Positive (increase in default rates)**

**Reasoning:**
- The treatment here is crossing the credit score threshold and being **approved for a loan**. Only individuals who receive loans can default on them.
- Individuals just above the cutoff gain access to credit, which mechanically gives them the *ability* to default, while those just below are denied and cannot default.
- This creates a **positive discontinuity** in default rates at the cutoff — a jump upward when moving from below to above the threshold.

**Expected magnitude:**
- The default rate variable `y` appears to range roughly from 0 to ~0.5 based on the preview. I would expect a LATE of approximately **0.15–0.30** (15–30 percentage points), reflecting the fact that gaining loan access exposes borrowers near the margin to default risk.
- These marginal borrowers (near the cutoff) are typically higher-risk, which could push the effect toward the upper end of this range.

**Robustness expectations:**
- The McCrary test should show no manipulation (p > 0.05) if the credit score is not easily gamed near the threshold.
- The estimate should be relatively stable across bandwidths and polynomial orders.
- Placebo tests at false cutoffs should yield insignificant results, confirming the discontinuity is specific to the true threshold.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The analysis exploits the discontinuity at the credit score threshold to identify the causal effect.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Crossing the credit score threshold increases the default rate.
